title: Effects of proton beam therapy on blood coagulation in patients with malignant head and neck cancer: A monocentric exploratory study
summary: Proton therapy is an innovative form of cancer treatment in which high-precision radiation is used to treat tumors while sparing the surrounding healthy tissue as much as possible. Our research project is investigating how proton therapy affects the blood coagulation system in patients with head and neck tumors. The study focuses on coagulation-specific parameters and the jugular vein, which is located in the radiation field and may be altered by the radiation. To find this out, we are analyzing the patients' blood and performing ultrasound examinations of the jugular vein. The results of our study could not only improve the safety of proton therapy, but also provide new insights into the effects of radiotherapy on the blood coagulation system. This is important in order to optimize the treatment of tumor patients and to identify and avoid potential risks at an early stage.
conditions: malignant head and neck tumors in adult

interventions.name:

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
o Age ≥ 18 years at the start of proton therapy
o Diagnosis of a malignant head and neck tumor 
o PT at the WPE with justifying indication and consent for PT targeting the primary tumor and the bilateral/ipsilateral lymphatic drainage pathways
o Participation in the WPE adult registry study (ProReg) with corresponding consent (12-5143-BO, ethics vote 21.08.2012)
o Signed declaration of consent for the study
Exclusion criteria:
o Age under 18 years
o Adjuvant radiotherapy concept
o Previous partial or complete neck dissection with removal of the internal jugular vein in the radiation area (surgery)
o Ongoing anticoagulation therapy
o Known thrombocytopathy
o Severe anemia with signs of ischemia
o Hormonal contraception
o No written consent for the WPE registry and the prospective study
